Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps on the GDPR/DPA items we discussed:

- Redwood is comfortable signing a standard DPA and can present SCC module options (we support the full set of EU SCC modules; for your use case we typically map to Modules 2 and 3 but happy to align).
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in Q4 2026. I have attached the SOC 2 summary and our DPA draft for your legal team to review.
- Controller/Processor: Based on what you shared, Acme Health will be the Controller and Redwood will act as a Processor for customer data processed through our hosted inference. If you have alternate data flows (e.g., you uploading datasets for model fine-tuning), we should flag those separately.

Next steps:
1) I have attached a DPA draft and a short SCC module mapping doc please share with Tom/legal and the security team.
2) Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk the SCC mapping and confirm controller/processor alignment? I'm available Tue/Wed afternoon PST.
3) If you'd like, I can start the vendor security questionnaire and loop our security lead (Rishi) for detailed answers.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf (DPA draft), SCC_module_mapping.xlsx (SCC module recommendations)

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alice,

Quick answers to your security questions:

- Telemetry logs: Request metadata and transient telemetry used for routing and debugging are treated as operational/technical logs. We can treat request metadata as Processor data within the DPA scope if you prefer our standard DPA includes telemetry in the definition of Personal Data when it is linked to a natural person.
- SCC modules: In your scenario (Acme = Controller in EU, Redwood = Processor in US), Module 2 is typically appropriate. In the SCC mapping spreadsheet I attached the recommended clause-by-clause mapping and fallback options when subprocessors are involved.
- SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II covers ingestion, storage, and inference serving layers. Third-party subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring vendors) are enumerated in Annex B of the SOC 2 summary; we can provide a redacted list for procurement review.

Happy to join the call and walk through specifics. Marissa -- I'll prepare short answers for the vendor questionnaire and flag any items that need engineering input.

- Rishi
